newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran, U.N. body trade charges over refugee housing.
newsitem.headline: Iran, U.N. body trade charges over refugee housing.

text.p: Iran and the United Nations refugee agency on Tuesday exchanged charges over blame for delays in providing winter housing for 27,000 Iraqi Kurdish refugees sheltering in tent camps in Iran.

"With the start of the cold season...$10 million is needed for prefabricated houses, which the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees has not taken any steps to provide despite repeated reminders by Iran," said Ahmad Hosseini, Iran's top official in charge of refugees, quoted by state-run Tehran radio.

Hosseini, quoted by the Iranian news agency IRNA, said: "The UNHCR has so far paid $3.1 million to Iran which is highly insufficient in the light of the $15 million needed to cover the current expenses of the refugees."
But a UNHCR official in Tehran blamed the delays on Iran.

"It is two months that UNHCR has untiredly raised the issue of relocation with Iranian authorities and there has been throughout absence of concrete signals that they are willing to proceed with relocation," Laurens Jolles said by telephone.
The U.N. agency has asked Tehran to move the refugees from cold mountainous areas to warmer regions in Iran.

"UNHCR has mentioned some criteria of speediness and cost-effectiveness of building prefabs and the very late proposal from Iran does not meet these criteria, in particular regarding speediness," Jolles said.
Hosseini said there were still 27,000 refugees sheltering at three camps in Iran after 48,000 of the original 75,000 returned voluntarily to five camps inside Iraq, IRNA reported.
The refugees fled fighting between rival Kurdish factions in northern Iraq which erupted in late August.
